label: Ambiguous Emergency
summary: Knee MRI above the prior-auth threshold, no authorization, emergency status unknown.
watch: An emergency exemption might apply, but the emergency status is unknown. Watch the system refuse to guess and name the missing fact.

label: Emergency Confirmed
summary: The same claim after the analyst confirms the emergency and the 72h retro-authorization request.
watch: Run this right after the ambiguous case: the missing facts are supplied, and the evidence-backed decision changes.

label: Obvious Approval
summary: Routine lipid panel for an active member. No prior authorization needed.
watch: Every check passes and the model agrees, so an autonomous approval is allowed.

label: Missing Authorization
summary: Knee MRI above the threshold, no authorization, documented as non-emergency.
watch: The rules fail and no exemption applies. The denial cites the exact policy version.

label: Policy Conflict
summary: Northeast member: the regional addendum and national policy disagree on the threshold.
watch: The deterministic rule engine detects the conflict and blocks any autonomous decision.

label: Possible Duplicate
summary: Knee MRI with a valid authorization, 11 days after an identical paid claim.
watch: Claims history finds the duplicate. The second retrieval pass then pulls in the duplicate-claims policy.

label: High-Value Claim
summary: A $14,500 knee arthroscopy with authorization on file.
watch: The rules pass, but high-value claims are never approved autonomously.

label: Incomplete Claim
summary: Physical therapy claim with no billed amount and no diagnosis code.
watch: Missing data is a business outcome: the claim is escalated and the missing fields are listed.
